text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

Two of Poland's three sugar-industry banks, Poznzan-based Bank Rozwoju Cukrownictwa and Wroclaw-based Bank Cukrownictwa Cukrobank, are holding talks aimed at finding a strategic investor. They are considering forming a holding led by a larger bank.

Ford predicts that by the year 2006 annual car demand in Poland will reach 500,000 cars, putting the country in sixth place in Europe. This year Poles are expected to buy 300,000 cars, one third of them on credit.
Bakers say bread and roll prices could rise up to 60 percent this year, though some analysts see rises of only 10 to 15 percent.
The National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, seeks quick sales of banks Prosper Bank, Polski Bank Inwestycyjny (PBI) and Pierwszy Komercyjny Bank (PBK).
Marek Borowski, deputy parliament speaker and a senior official of the co-ruling Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), said income taxes will likely be lowered in 1998, not next year.

The bourse on Wednesday will consider whether to approve for bourse trade sharesissues of the wood and furniture trader Paged, the Zasada automotive group, the Kompap paper firm and the Ariel shoe firm.
The Sokolow meat producer plans by the end of the year to raise to a majority stake its share in the Kolo meat factory, which seeks a bourse listing next year.
